title: Sepalith 72-hour model campaign task board
deadline: After training coverage and development selection; calendar cutoffs superseded by user (LEAD-all-eligible-data-policy-20260914.json)

phases.title: Prepare and protect the lane
phases.goal: Pin sources, preserve the live O2 control, establish one-CUDA ownership, storage, provider and recovery rules.

phases.title: Freeze the prediction-time prompt contract
phases.goal: Make Python, TypeScript, SFT and RL receive the same prediction-time information and measured length/stop contract.

phases.title: Build clean train, dev and final registries
phases.window: Sat 00:00–12:00 in parallel with prompt work
phases.goal: Create package-disjoint, validator-backed, tokenizer-audited registries without legacy evaluation leakage.

phases.title: Train one broad MiniCPM SFT parent
phases.goal: Run the single Midtrain primary, preserve checkpoints and select one immutable theta0.

phases.title: Run sustained parent-specific RL
phases.goal: Run one measured broad-mixture GRPO trajectory with durable checkpoints and held-out development gates.

phases.title: Use conditional independent capacity
phases.goal: Use Anyscale primarily for same-parent breadth SFT; keep Azure/Kaggle conditional and non-blocking.

phases.title: Co-optimize serving architecture
phases.window: Sat 00:00–Tue 09:00, early fixtures and late finalist checks
phases.goal: Measure host placement, cache/context behavior and competing target/draft coupling while training proceeds.

phases.title: Freeze, validate and deliver
phases.window: Mon 00:00–Tue 09:00; final set opens after Mon 12:00
phases.goal: Select by development, open the locked final only after freeze, package Q8, runtime and rollback evidence, and deliver.

tasks.title: Snapshot authoritative sources and artifacts
tasks.summary: Capture the exact dirty worktree, owner worktree, canonical asset roots, model revisions and required uncommitted fixes before any launch.
steps: Record git SHAs, worktree paths and dirty-file manifests for the plan checkout, active owner checkout and canonical assets.
Hash the current plan, prompt contract, runner, training entry points and existing release artifacts.
Write a source map that distinguishes readable evidence from files that must not be regenerated.
acceptance: The manifest names all three roots and records their SHAs or dirty state.
Every planned launch can resolve its source, model and environment from the manifest.
No source or artifact is modified by the inventory.
tasks.stopRule: Stop if any required root or dirty fix cannot be identified; use the existing b4 fallback until resolved.
tasks.gate: Required before training, cloud packaging or release packaging.

tasks.title: Establish one-CUDA ownership and process ledger
tasks.summary: Audit the 5090 and reserve one owner at a time, explicitly separating the live O2 control from the finished filtered arm.
steps: Record nvidia-smi memory/utilization, active PIDs and command lines.
Identify PID 1700431 as the O2 unfiltered control when present and record its output directory.
Create a handoff rule that forbids a second CUDA workload until the owner releases the device.
acceptance: The live control and finished O2-filtered artifact have distinct IDs and paths.
The ledger has one current GPU owner and a next-slot condition.
No second dispatcher or training process is started.
tasks.stopRule: Stop any new GPU launch while an unregistered process or the active control owns the device.

tasks.title: Recheck storage and artifact headroom
tasks.summary: Measure current storage before copying checkpoints, preserving the current root reading and separately flagging the historical full-snapshot estimate for recheck.
steps: Run a fresh df/du inventory for the workspace, /mnt/e, /mnt/h and NAS destinations.
Record the current root reading of approximately 103 GiB free only if the live measurement agrees; do not reuse an unverified historical snapshot.
Identify disposable build outputs without deleting anything and reserve durable paths for light/full checkpoints.
acceptance: A timestamped storage receipt reports measured free space and shared-file caveats.
The historical full-snapshot size is marked unverified until remeasured.
No research, active-run or environment files are deleted.
tasks.stopRule: Stop cleanup when ownership or artifact provenance is uncertain; stage to /mnt/e or NAS instead.
tasks.gate: Required before checkpoint copying or export.

tasks.title: Check provider admission and credit limits
tasks.summary: Resolve account readiness before reserving paid capacity, distinguishing Anyscale authentication from Azure Cost Management authorization and Kaggle quota.
steps: Check Anyscale authentication, available A10G allocation and lifecycle/shutdown capability without starting training.
Check Azure subscription and Cost Management once; record AADSTS530035 or the current result without retries.
Read Kaggle GPU quota/reset state and write provider-specific ceilings and abort contacts.
acceptance: Anyscale auth state and a bounded cost/lifecycle plan are recorded, or the lane is explicitly disabled.
Azure is marked blocked unless its Cost Management check succeeds, and that disabled result is usable by the local plan.
Kaggle is explicitly optional and cannot gate delivery.
tasks.stopRule: Do not launch paid compute when auth, cost ceiling or independent termination is unverified.
tasks.gate: Required admission check; provider branches remain conditional.

tasks.title: Pin software, hardware and tokenizer environment
tasks.summary: Record the exact runtime needed to reproduce the primary SFT/RL and serving artifacts.
steps: Capture Python, PyTorch, Transformers, TRL, Unsloth, PEFT, Datasets, llama.cpp and CUDA/driver versions.
Record RTX 5090, host RAM, target-host identities and model/tokenizer cache locations.
Pin or snapshot the environment without upgrading dependencies during a run.
acceptance: A manifest contains exact package versions and hardware identity.
The active runner and SFT entry point resolve to the pinned source.
Any version mismatch is an explicit gate failure.
tasks.stopRule: Stop a launch if the installed stack differs from the manifest and cannot be reproduced in a smoke.
tasks.gate: Required for every training and export task.

tasks.title: Freeze the 66-GPU-hour calendar and cut rules
tasks.summary: Translate the authoritative budget into executable windows without treating engineer time as GPU time.
steps: Record 8 GPU-hours for the existing control, 12 for primary SFT, 26 for RL, 4 for consolidation, 10 for evaluation/harness and 6 for export/recovery.
Set RL stop at Monday 00:00 Berlin and weight/harness freeze at Monday 12:00.
Order cuts as optional branches, merges/consolidation and extra probes before final validation.
acceptance: The local ledger sums to exactly 66 GPU-hours.
No required release task depends on cloud or optional experiments.
The ledger records wall-clock cutoffs separately from compute ceilings.
tasks.stopRule: Stop optional launches when the remaining wall window or GPU budget cannot cover export and final validation.

tasks.title: Archive the O2 control and filtered comparator separately
tasks.summary: Allow the running PID 1700431 control to finish, then preserve its receipt without relabeling the completed O2-filtered run as a control.
tasks.effort: 0.5 engineer-hour; up to 8 RTX 5090 GPU-hours already allocated to the control
steps: Monitor the existing control only and collect its terminal metrics, checkpoints and command line.
Evaluate control and filtered artifacts on the declared common battery with separate denominators.
Write a comparison ledger naming filtered, unfiltered and banked b4 rows.
acceptance: The receipt identifies the control PID/output and its terminal state.
The 255/307 filtered result is labeled finished filtered, while the control result is separately labeled unfiltered.
No new O2 run is launched.
tasks.stopRule: Stop comparison if the battery, denominator or model lineage differs; report the artifact as unavailable rather than merging labels.

tasks.title: Prepare the b4 rollback and banked artifact ledger
tasks.summary: Make a tested fallback available before the new lineage consumes the release window.
steps: Locate and hash b4 Q8_0, its launch settings, parser/marker contract and any O2/Spark/Granite comparator artifacts.
Write a fresh-start and already-running-sidecar rollback command without changing private research files.
Record which comparator metrics are historical and which must be re-evaluated on the new development set.
acceptance: A b4 artifact, hash and launch recipe are present.
Rollback can run independently of the MiniCPM lineage.
Historical scores carry explicit cohort and denominator labels.
tasks.stopRule: Stop release packaging if the fallback hash or parser contract cannot be reproduced.

tasks.title: Create local tracker and hosted readable campaign snapshot
tasks.summary: Keep an interactive persistent tracker locally and a readable expandable snapshot for hosted viewing; do not add a PostPlanCSP script.
steps: Render this task board into a hosted-readable snapshot with all task details expanded or expandable.
Maintain the local tracker as the authoritative interactive state, with dependency and gate views.
Record board version, generation time and the rule that task status is maintained outside this immutable pending board.
acceptance: The hosted snapshot is readable without a custom CSP script.
The local tracker preserves task details and dependency links across updates.
The board does not invent completed status for audited historical work.
tasks.stopRule: Stop if a tracker would overwrite the immutable task definitions; create a new revision receipt instead.
tasks.gate: Optional administrative surface; it must not block prompt, data, SFT or release work.

tasks.title: Freeze representative pre-edit event fixtures
tasks.summary: Build non-final snapshots that exercise the information available at prediction time before changing the renderer.
steps: Collect typing, deletion, cursor movement, history append/eviction, diagnostic refresh, definition change, anchor move and file-switch episodes.
Include long-scope, cross-file, local-only, evidence-missing and no-op cases.
Record source provenance and ensure every snapshot is pre-edit and outside the locked final set.
acceptance: Fixtures cover all named event classes with pre-edit context and target geometry.
No target, post-edit repository state or future intent is used to construct an input.
Each fixture has a stable ID and source package.
tasks.stopRule: Stop a fixture if its context can only be reconstructed from post-edit state; quarantine it for audit.

tasks.title: Map Python and TypeScript renderer gaps
tasks.summary: Compare the live extension, shared contract and training renderer so SFT does not teach fields serving cannot supply.
steps: Inspect suffix/prefix/outline/region ordering, history/evidence fields, character caps and cursor offset conventions.
List every missing provider and every field whose value differs between Python and TypeScript.
Separate host-side provenance metadata from model-visible prompt text.
acceptance: A gap matrix names each mismatch and its owner.
The matrix includes the live lack of history/diagnostic/retrieved-definition rendering.
No unsupported field is silently added to the new training schema.
tasks.stopRule: Stop if a field has no prediction-time provider; represent it as missing rather than idealized context.

tasks.title: Specify the versioned prompt schema and output contract
tasks.summary: Define model-visible sections, order, missing-field semantics and unchanged replacement/output semantics before SFT.
steps: Define the fixed task contract, workspace-relative path, current prefix/region/scope, selected evidence, history/diagnostics, suffix and generation boundary.
Assign a renderer ID and version all section delimiters, special-token handling and output markers.
Keep audit metadata outside the prompt unless its model-visible use is justified.
acceptance: The schema has one explicit field order and an empty-section policy.
The replacement/output terminator semantics remain compatible with the parser.
The schema forbids timestamps, global hashes and future edit intent at the prompt head.
tasks.stopRule: Stop if the schema cannot preserve exact whitespace, cursor geometry or complete targets.

tasks.title: Build shared literal, tokenizer and output fixtures
tasks.summary: Make Python training, evaluation, RL and TypeScript serving agree on boundaries, Unicode, BOS/EOS and marker handling.
steps: Test Unicode cursor offsets, whitespace, replacement boundaries, missing evidence and literal marker-like source text.
Tokenize prompt plus target and serving overhead with the chosen tokenizer, including BOS/EOS treatment.
Round-trip generated output through the parser and application fixture.
acceptance: Python and TypeScript produce matching fixture IDs, boundaries and marker behavior.
Complete targets plus terminal tokens fit the recorded admission budget.
Known-correct, known-wrong and no-op fixtures produce distinct parser outcomes.
tasks.stopRule: Stop if a boundary or marker mismatch would make training labels differ from serving application.

tasks.title: Implement prediction-time context selection and dropout
tasks.summary: Provide current source, bounded history and deterministic evidence while preserving missing-provider and evidence-dependent cases.
steps: Select unsaved current source, exact cursor/region, enclosing scope and bounded chronological history.
Add relevant definitions/signatures, fresh diagnostics and related tests only when a provider supplies them.
Apply fixed optional-evidence dropout only when the target remains supported, and leave unsupported rows out.
acceptance: A renderer can produce current-source-only, evidence-present and missing-evidence prompts.
History never derives from the target and stale evidence is omitted or refreshed.
Selection and truncation anchors are deterministic and provenance-backed.
tasks.stopRule: Stop if a provider leaks post-edit state or an evidence dropout removes the only support for a target.

tasks.title: Compare at most three prompt layouts on identical snapshots
tasks.summary: Use the pre-SFT harness budget to compare suffix-first control, file-prefix-first and stable-reference-first with the same selected information.
tasks.effort: 1 engineer-hour; up to 2 RTX 5090 GPU-hours, serialized
steps: Render each fixture under the three layouts without changing evidence, labels or target.
Measure token common-prefix survival and recomputation requirements across event types.
Confirm promising layouts with pinned-server prompt timing, recording backend and contention.
acceptance: All layouts use the same snapshot IDs and selected information.
The receipt separates token-overlap diagnostics from measured latency.
One primary layout and the legacy fallback are nominated before SFT.
tasks.stopRule: Stop the comparison after the third layout or when the two-GPU-hour allocation is consumed; do not start full SFT arms.

tasks.title: Profile SFT/RL lengths and the 480/170 memory workaround
tasks.summary: Measure tokenizer lengths and a small memory/throughput profile instead of treating the short current caps as a quality hypothesis.
tasks.effort: 1 engineer-hour; up to 0.5 RTX 5090 GPU-hour, serialized
steps: Tokenize representative fixtures and targets under MiniCPM, reporting the current dataset filters of 480 prompt and 170 target tokens.
Profile the SFT proposal of 80% <=2048 total tokens and up to 20% naturally longer <=4096 examples.
Profile RL candidates up to 2048 prompt plus 192 completion tokens, reducing simultaneous rollout generation if needed rather than deleting evidence.
acceptance: The receipt distinguishes dataset 480/170 filters, old RL trainer 512/192 limits and the proposed longer profile.
No profile removes target tokens or critical evidence to satisfy a cap.
Peak memory, generated tokens and throughput are recorded for each admitted bucket.
tasks.stopRule: Stop a longer profile if memory or policy-log-probability support is not validated; retain the smaller correct profile.
tasks.gate: Required before primary SFT and RL manifest.

tasks.title: Freeze the pre-SFT prompt contract
tasks.summary: Select one renderer layout, context policy, dropout policy and output contract for broad SFT, with a correct smaller fallback if optional providers are absent.
steps: Choose the primary renderer ID and record the legacy fallback.
Freeze selected evidence ordering, history limits, tokenizer budget, marker semantics and empty optional sections.
Publish the contract manifest to the SFT/data handoff.
acceptance: Exactly one layout is marked primary before SFT launch.
The contract can render a valid prompt when every optional provider is missing.
No full SFT contest or unsupported retrieval dependency remains on the critical path.
tasks.stopRule: Stop SFT admission if Python, TypeScript and RL fixture IDs do not agree with the frozen contract.

tasks.title: Prepare the prompt contract handoff and rollout checklist
tasks.summary: Make the frozen renderer, length buckets and stop contract consumable by data, SFT and RL tasks.
steps: Record renderer ID, tokenizer revision, prompt/output caps and length-bucket IDs in one handoff manifest.
List pre-RL checks for cache/fresh correctness, no-op reward, cap hits, parser and stop behavior.
Define a new stage ID for any later prompt or length change.
acceptance: SFT and RL manifests can reference one immutable prompt handoff.
A changed field/order cannot silently reuse an old stage ID.
The checklist names every required pre-RL observation.
tasks.stopRule: Stop handoff if the actual tokenizer or renderer cannot be pinned.
tasks.gate: Required dependency for data and training.

tasks.title: Inventory all data packs, environments and lineage
tasks.summary: Catalog rows, packages, trajectories, source identities and validators before constructing new splits.
steps: Enumerate SFT, RL, B11, SY1, scenario, trajectory and environment sources with file hashes.
Record family, package/repository, source parent, target, validator and derivation metadata.
Mark known teacher-selection, post-training, banked and paper-derived sources.
acceptance: Every admitted source has a provenance record and family label.
Known post-training and historical evaluation sources are identifiable.
The inventory preserves raw inputs without mutation.
tasks.stopRule: Stop admission for rows without provenance or a recoverable target/context boundary.

tasks.title: Build one global package/repository split
tasks.summary: Assign package/repository groups consistently across SFT, RL, development, final and all derived twins.
steps: Group rows by canonical package/repository, source parent and fork/alias identity.
Exclude the full sft_v7 package set and known post-training sources from the clean final candidate pool.
Keep complete trajectories together and prevent one source edit from crossing train/dev/final.
acceptance: A split manifest has disjoint package/repository groups and source aliases.
The legacy sft_v3/eval file, inspected derivatives and historical scenario batteries are excluded from final.
Every later registry references this split ID.
tasks.stopRule: Stop if a package cannot be resolved or if a final candidate is derived from post-training evaluation material.

tasks.title: Audit contradictions, duplicates and target visibility
tasks.summary: Remove irreducible labels and rows whose target cannot be derived from prediction-time evidence.
steps: Find identical normalized prompts with conflicting targets and exact/full-text duplicates across splits.
Check that pre-edit context, target and validator are separately recoverable.
Quarantine TU3's 28 contradictory prompt/target pairs and severe truncation until repaired.
acceptance: The collision receipt lists every contradictory pair and quarantine reason.
No contradictory prompt reaches a required training or final manifest.
Rows lacking visible target support are tagged rather than relabeled.
tasks.stopRule: Stop a family if its validator or target boundary is ambiguous; do not fill quotas with guessed labels.

tasks.title: Run candidate-tokenizer length and target audit
tasks.summary: Recompute eligibility under the selected MiniCPM tokenizer and frozen prompt contract, including current filters and proposed long buckets.
steps: Encode prompts, complete targets and terminal tokens under the actual tokenizer.
Report rows dropped by the current 480/170 builder filters and rows that fit the proposed 2048/4096 SFT or 2048+192 RL profiles.
Keep prompt and target token counts separate and record family/source losses.
acceptance: The receipt provides per-family eligible counts and exact drop reasons.
No row is admitted by truncating a target or required evidence.
The profile decision can update filters and rollout configuration together.
tasks.stopRule: Stop the long bucket if it only contains duplicated examples or cannot retain full targets.

tasks.title: Build the cleaned SFT registry
tasks.summary: Materialize one broad train registry from lossless, validator-backed rows under the global split and frozen prompt contract.
steps: Convert structured rows through the shared renderer, preserving observed context, target and marker.
Include real edits/completions, deterministic repairs, documented tasks, comment/doc tasks and checked no-ops.
Exclude TU3, contradictory rows, legacy final sources and rows failing full-target eligibility.
acceptance: Every registry row links to source, package, renderer ID, tokenizer profile and target hash.
No post-edit context or final-set failure is used to author a training target.
The registry reports family and length coverage.
tasks.stopRule: Stop conversion for any row that fails round-trip rendering; quarantine it with a reason.

tasks.title: Implement the parameterized SFT sampler
tasks.summary: Use 10% no-op slots and square-root family allocation with a 25% ceiling, backfilling only from eligible replay.
steps: Compute quotas from admitted family counts rather than old fixed pools.
Reserve 10% no-op slots, cap any family at 25%, cap new small-pack source rows at three presentations and backfill unavailable slots.
Emit the exact selected IDs, draws, exposures and achieved mixture for each seed.
acceptance: The sampler produces a manifest without hard-coded run2/O2 assumptions.
No rare-family quota is met by indefinite duplication.
The 48,000-draw/3,000-update first readout can be reproduced from the manifest.
tasks.stopRule: Stop if the sampler cannot fill a quota with valid rows; renormalize and record the deficit.

tasks.title: Build the development selector panel
tasks.summary: Create a package-separated 128-case panel for checkpoint selection with edits, completions, no-ops and family labels.
steps: Sample 128 non-final cases from disjoint packages and trajectories.
Include family, length bucket, evidence-present/missing and no-op strata with verified targets.
Write scoring rules for exact, semantic/useful edit, parser, no-op false suggestion and cap hits.
acceptance: The panel has no package or normalized-prompt collision with training.
Every case has a validator or declared human review path.
The panel can be scored repeatedly without opening the locked final set.
tasks.stopRule: Stop if the panel cannot reach declared coverage; report the actual package count and uncertainty.

tasks.title: Build and lock the final evaluation manifest
tasks.summary: Construct the 600–1000-point final set from at least 30 independent packages where available, then keep it unopened until Monday 12:00.
steps: Select useful edits, deterministic repairs, no-edits and realistic typing/history events from clean sources.
Exclude sft_v3/eval, its overlap-derived rows, sft_v7 packages, historical batteries and all post-training/teacher-selection sources.
Hash the manifest, restrict routine access and create a separate 2K/4K plus 8K stress trace manifest.
acceptance: The final manifest records package/repository disjointness and source exclusions.
The final data remains unopened until the declared weight/harness freeze.
Shortfall from 600–1000 or 30 packages is reported rather than padded with leaked rows.
tasks.stopRule: Stop if final rows derive from training, historical evaluation or post-edit state; use a smaller honest final set.

tasks.title: Build the parent-specific RL pool and verifier manifest
tasks.summary: Create broad RL quotas and validators for the selected parent without inheriting the b4/O2 prescreen or stale 480/170 admissions.
steps: Parameterize primary quotas around rename, format, no-op, pipe and validated additional/finish families from available rows.
Run known-correct/known-wrong/no-op verifier fixtures and retain evidence-dependent tasks only when evidence is visible.
Record the actual prompt/target profile, 192-token completion maximum and any rows excluded by the chosen rollout profile.
acceptance: The manifest has no hard-coded O2/run2 filter and names the selected parent/renderer/tokenizer.
Every admitted row has a passing verifier or an explicit SFT-only tag.
TU3 and contradictory rows are absent.
tasks.stopRule: Stop RL pool assembly if verifier pass/fail cannot distinguish a correct no-op from parser failure.

tasks.title: Load and audit the MiniCPM Midtrain checkpoint
tasks.summary: Verify the pinned revision, tokenizer and architecture before committing the 12-hour SFT slot.
steps: Load the pinned `openbmb/MiniCPM5-2B-Midtrain` revision with the selected tokenizer.
Inspect model type, trainable projection names, vocabulary, BOS/EOS IDs and chat-template behavior.
Run one prompt/target fixture through the frozen renderer and model loader.
acceptance: The model loads without GDN-specific assumptions or unexpected offload.
The two EOS IDs and special-token behavior are recorded.
The fixture reports prompt/target lengths under the chosen SFT profile.
tasks.stopRule: Stop the Midtrain primary if architecture, tokenizer or memory behavior is incompatible; consider the final checkpoint only as a reserve decision.

tasks.title: Attach SFT LoRA and run the 50-step smoke
tasks.summary: Verify actual modules, finite loss, renderer compatibility, export and throughput before the primary SFT.
steps: Attach the audited MiniCPM projection list at r32/alpha64 with BF16 and effective batch 16.
Run 50 updates using the frozen prompt contract and candidate length buckets.
Export a temporary adapter and run parser/output/target round-trip fixtures.
acceptance: Loss is finite and trainable module count matches the audit.
No persistent system-memory fallback or unexpected OOM occurs.
Exported output tokenizes, parses and preserves the target contract.
tasks.stopRule: Stop the primary launch after OOM, nonfinite loss, dropped target, parser mismatch or unmeasured throughput.

tasks.title: Launch broad SFT and verify the first update
tasks.summary: Start the one broad SFT trajectory, verify its identity and first healthy optimizer update, then hand monitoring to the checkpoint tasks while the job continues.
steps: Confirm the SFT smoke, resumable checkpoint hooks, selected renderer and data registry receipts.
Acquire the single CUDA lease and start the pinned run toward the initial 3000-update readout within the 12-hour ceiling.
Record PID, command, source/model/data hashes, output directory, first valid update and the next evaluation checkpoint. Leave terminal completion to SFT-10.
acceptance: A launch receipt identifies the actual running process and first finite-loss update.
Checkpoint and development callbacks are active before the long run proceeds.
The run has one resource owner and a declared deadline; launch acceptance does not claim training completion.
tasks.stopRule: Stop at the first unresolved OOM, target truncation, data leakage or calendar overrun; preserve the best valid checkpoint.

tasks.title: Install SFT checkpoint, resume and evaluation hooks
tasks.summary: Make checkpoint persistence, interruption/resume and early development reads ready before the primary SFT starts.
tasks.effort: 0.25 engineer-hour; included in SFT-03's 12 GPU-hour job
steps: Configure lightweight adapter/config snapshots, full optimizer/scheduler/RNG/sampler state, durable output paths and retention before launch.
Install the development evaluator callback so it can consume checkpoints as they appear without waiting for the terminal run.
Run an interrupted 50-step resume dry-run and verify optimizer, scheduler, RNG and sampler restoration.
acceptance: The primary launch can name save/resume/evaluation paths before SFT-03 starts.
The dry-run restores state rather than starting a fresh optimizer.
The evaluator can read an available checkpoint while the full SFT remains in progress.
tasks.stopRule: Stop the primary launch if durable save, resume or early-evaluation hooks cannot be exercised in the smoke.

tasks.title: Record the first scheduled SFT development readout
tasks.summary: Evaluate the first saved SFT checkpoint while the trajectory is running; later periodic reads remain part of the terminal SFT archive.
tasks.effort: 1.5 engineer-hours; up to 2 compute-hours on validated CPU/cloud backend
steps: At the first scheduled saved checkpoint, pause or hand off the CUDA lease safely, or use an available compatible evaluator.
Score the fixed development panel with per-family edit, no-op, target-length and evidence-use results.
Record the readout and resume/stop recommendation; schedule subsequent evaluations through SFT-10 without opening the final set.
acceptance: The first scheduled checkpoint has a complete development report with denominators and model/renderer/data identities.
The next evaluation and any stopping concern are recorded.
No final-test row was used, and this receipt does not claim later checkpoints have been evaluated.
tasks.stopRule: Stop additional SFT scoring when the evaluation allowance or data boundary would be breached.

tasks.title: Run bounded source-supported finish correction
tasks.summary: Correct verified incomplete finish targets using a fresh SFT stage from selected theta0, then choose continuation from fixed development milestones.
tasks.effort: Up to1 compute-hour reallocated from unused RL ceiling
steps: Verify versioned corrected TRAIN and DEV artifacts, preserving original sources and no-op mixture.

Original full-text50/100 arm was cut. Admit one fresh target-only25 pilot from theta0 at LR5e-5 with fixed200-step schedule horizon, target+EOS masks and pre-update objective check; any full25-to50 resume requires a new root decision.
Choose continuation or stop from actual editing/no-op,finish application,protocol and latency evidence.
acceptance: Corrected inputs bind exact source and tokenizer identities with no truncated targets.
Full checkpoint,optimizer,RNG,sampler and development readouts are verified at every decision.
No automatic continuation or promotion; fallback and final-set seal remain.
tasks.stopRule: Stop fresh pilot25, runtime/memory gate failure, remaining1775.576667825all-in seconds, or Monday00Berlin. No automatic resume; later target-only50 is unconditional ceiling.
tasks.gate: Conditional source-supported correction replaces deferred optional selector work.

tasks.title: Extend the primary SFT only when the gate earns it
tasks.summary: Use unused eligible data and development retention to decide whether to continue toward 6,000 updates/96,000 draws.
tasks.effort: 0.25 engineer-hour; uses only remaining SFT allocation within the 12 GPU-hour ceiling
steps: Check measured throughput, development retention and remaining calendar before extending.
Resume the same schedule when possible; if a new optimizer/schedule is used, assign a new stage ID.
Archive the extension and compare it with the selected 3,000-update checkpoint.
acceptance: The extension stays within 12 GPU-hours and does not delay RL.
No repeated cosine restart is presented as a faithful continuation.
A development decision says extend or keep the shorter checkpoint.
tasks.stopRule: Stop extension at the first retention regression, calendar conflict or budget exhaustion.
tasks.gate: Conditional; never required for RL admission.

tasks.title: Select one SFT checkpoint for the common parent
tasks.summary: Choose the SFT checkpoint that will seed every decisive branch using development quality, restraint, length and export evidence.
steps: Rank valid SFT checkpoints using the development report and optional diagnostic evidence.
Check no-op, target support, parser, length and target-host feasibility against b4.
Record one selected checkpoint and one fallback without opening the final set.
acceptance: Exactly one checkpoint is designated `theta0` input.
The selection receipt contains metrics, denominators, source and renderer hashes.
No optional extension or cloud branch is required to define theta0.
tasks.stopRule: Stop selection if all checkpoints fail the smoke or development validity gates; use b4 while repairing.

tasks.title: Merge and hash the immutable theta0 parent
tasks.summary: Create one durable merged Midtrain→SFT parent with tokenizer and serving contract for all branches.
steps: Merge the selected adapter into a durable non-/tmp directory using explicit model and tokenizer paths.
Hash merged weights, tokenizer, renderer ID, marker protocol and environment manifest.
Run a load/generation/parser fixture and preserve the unmodified SFT adapter separately.
acceptance: The hash and parent path reproduce the selected checkpoint exactly.
Every subsequent branch can reference the same theta0 bytes.
The b4 rollback remains independent.
tasks.stopRule: Stop branch packaging if merge changes tokenizer, special tokens or parser behavior.
tasks.gate: Hard gate for RL and same-parent cloud.

tasks.title: Finalize SFT and archive its checkpoint history
tasks.summary: Monitor the remaining primary SFT trajectory, perform scheduled development reads, and close the job with a durable checkpoint and terminal receipt.
tasks.effort: 0.25 engineer-hour; included in SFT-03's 12 GPU-hour job
steps: Maintain the 500-update adapter/full-state cadence and periodic development evaluations while the primary job runs.
At 3000 updates, record the stop or optional-extension decision against development results, measured throughput and the remaining 12-hour allowance.
Stop by the declared deadline, verify the real process has ended, and archive the checkpoint inventory, optimizer/RNG/sampler state, scores and final training-token counts.
acceptance: The process is terminal and its ending reason, update count and elapsed allocation are recorded.
Every scored checkpoint and the latest full resume state are recoverable by hash.
The complete available development history supports SFT-08 selecting a parent; missing or skipped evaluations are explicit.
tasks.stopRule: Stop continuation if the latest safe state cannot be copied or verified; use the last valid checkpoint.
tasks.gate: Required in-run monitor; launch it alongside SFT-03 and let it finish independently.

tasks.title: Parameterize the RL runner for theta0 and the chosen context profile
tasks.summary: Replace b4-specific paths and filters while retaining the first comparable GRPO reward and adapter geometry.
steps: Add explicit model, SFT adapter/merge, renderer, data, stop/EOS, prompt/completion, resume and output-path arguments.
Update the 480/170 dataset filters together with trainer/rollout limits; do not leave longer eligible rows silently excluded.
Add light-adapter and full-state checkpoint hooks, telemetry fields and a dry-run manifest.
acceptance: The runner has no hard-coded v6/b4 merge or O2 prescreen dependency.
A dry run resolves theta0, tokenizer, quotas, stop contract and output directory.
The first arm keeps exact-plus-0.2-line-F1, beta 0 and r16/alpha16 unless the smoke records a necessary change.
tasks.stopRule: Stop implementation if a change requires a framework migration or invalidates the existing reward parser.

tasks.title: Materialize the parent-specific RL pool and stage manifest
tasks.summary: Bind the validator-backed pool to theta0, renderer, length buckets and the measured rollout profile.
steps: Join admitted rows to theta0 tokenizer/renderer IDs and mark SFT-only rows.
Emit parameterized family quotas, no-op guard, source exposure cap and fallback backfill.
Record the candidate prompt maximum, 192-token completion maximum and expected completion/group counts.
acceptance: Every row has a parent-independent source and parent-specific eligibility result.
The manifest distinguishes proposed 2048+192 from the actually measured profile.
No final-set failures or O2-selected-only rows enter the required pool.
tasks.stopRule: Stop if the measured profile cannot retain complete targets or if a family has no valid reward contract.

tasks.title: Run the pre-RL theta0 behavior and rollout gate
tasks.summary: Validate evidence sensitivity, parser/stop parity, no-op reward and memory before the long trajectory.
tasks.effort: 1 engineer-hour; up to 1 RTX 5090 GPU-hour, serialized
steps: Compare correct, irrelevant/missing-evidence and local-only fixtures on theta0.
Run cache-enabled and fresh-state generation, no-op/marker fixtures and candidate length profiles.
Measure rollout memory, policy-log-probability path, cap hits and actual completion tokens.
acceptance: The chosen profile fits without silent truncation or missing loss-bearing probabilities.
Parser, stop, no-op and cache/fresh outputs satisfy the frozen contract.
A measured throughput and profile decision is recorded.
tasks.stopRule: Stop long RL if behavior, policy-log-probability, parser or memory gates fail; repair or fall back to theta0/b4.

tasks.title: Freeze the RL rollout, reward and quota manifest
tasks.summary: Make the long run's prompt length, output length, family mix, stop contract and stage identity immutable.
steps: Choose the measured prompt profile up to 2048 plus 192 and record any smaller memory-safe profile.
Freeze exact/line-F1 reward, four generations, batch/accumulation, beta, temperature, quotas and no-op guard.
Write the RL stage ID and explicit Monday 00:00 stop/cut rule.
acceptance: The manifest records actual rather than assumed prompt/completion limits.
A later profile or renderer change must receive a new stage ID.
The manifest names theta0 and all source/validator hashes.
tasks.stopRule: Stop if any reward, renderer, quota or length setting remains implicit.

tasks.title: Launch broad-mixture GRPO and hand off at first valid update
tasks.summary: Launch the instrumented broad-mixture GRPO job and hand off after its first valid update; RL-10 records terminal completion separately.
tasks.effort: 0.5 engineer-hour; up to 26 RTX 5090 GPU-hours including rollouts
steps: Launch one instrumented run with r16/alpha16, four generations, batch 8 × accumulation 4, BNPO/group scaling and the frozen reward.
Record the first valid update, 32 completions per update, actual generated tokens, prompt lengths, wall time and family telemetry.
Continue only under RL-08's decision and the Monday 00:00 cutoff; do not make launch success imply terminal completion.
acceptance: A durable launch/first-valid-update receipt exists; terminal status may remain pending.
The 26 GPU-hour ceiling and one-CUDA policy are respected.
The run does not consume final-set failures or silently change renderer/reward.
tasks.stopRule: Stop on persistent quality deterioration, invalid reward/termination behavior, no learning signal, calendar cutoff or budget exhaustion.
tasks.gate: Primary RL launch gate; it closes at first valid update, not at terminal completion.

tasks.title: Install RL checkpoint and telemetry hooks before launch
tasks.summary: Prepare light adapters, full resumable state, telemetry callbacks and durable paths before the long RL job begins.
tasks.effort: 0.5 engineer-hour; included in RL-05's 26 GPU-hour job
steps: Save full resumable adapter/optimizer/scheduler/RNG/sampler state every5 RL updates and at every controlled stop. The cadence follows interrupted runs that reached6 updates but retained only light5. Preserve prior light and full snapshots; measure storage after the first full5 save.
Add reward, family, length, cap, termination, zero-variance and gradient telemetry fields.
Run a dry-run save/resume check against theta0 before releasing the GPU to RL-05.
acceptance: RL-05 can start with save, resume, telemetry and durable output paths already configured.
The dry-run restores optimizer, scheduler, RNG and sampler state.
The hook receipt does not rely on save_total_limit=2 or /tmp survival.
tasks.stopRule: Stop the long launch if hooks cannot save and restore state in the dry-run.

tasks.title: Record the first scheduled RL development readout
tasks.summary: Evaluate the first scheduled saved RL checkpoint during the active run, then hand later checks to the continuation and terminal tasks.
tasks.effort: Included in the RL-05 local ceiling; evaluate serially in the one owned CUDA process.
steps: At update5 in the corrected full5 stage, record the full-state identity and evaluate the fixed accepted75-case DEV panel (43 edits,32 no-ops). Continue DEV at update25 and every25 updates; preserve early interrupted attempts as such.
Report per-family edit/no-op scores, cap hits, invalid parses and reward variation; compare with theta0 and the existing baseline.
Record the recommendation and next checkpoint; continue periodic monitoring through RL-08 and RL-10.
acceptance: The first scheduled readout has model-specific metrics and denominators, or an explicit early-stop receipt explains why that checkpoint was not reached.
A next readout and continuation concern are recorded without claiming future checkpoints are evaluated.
The locked final set remains unopened.
tasks.stopRule: Skip stale intermediate evaluation rather than pausing productive training indefinitely; preserve the skipped artifact list.

tasks.title: Make scheduled early and sustained RL continuation decisions
tasks.summary: Decide whether the primary RL trajectory has useful held-out signal and should continue to the Monday cutoff.
steps: Review the early5-update DEV readout before resuming, then review25 and decide continuation at100 and250 or the latest evaluated checkpoint within six trajectory hours, whichever arrives first. Counts are ceilings; use measured time and remaining budget.
Compare the best RL checkpoint with theta0 and b4 on the development panel.
Check format/rename learning, no-op restraint, termination/cap behavior and retention.
Record stop, continue or fallback with remaining wall/GPU budget.
acceptance: The decision has explicit metrics, denominators and a timestamp before continuation.
A failed gate leaves theta0 and b4 available.
Continuation never consumes locked final evaluation time.
tasks.stopRule: Stop on protocol/memory/reward-contract failure immediately. Stop persistent DEV deterioration or absent held-out progress by update250 or six trajectory hours, whichever arrives first; document smaller beneficial checkpoints and preserve theta0/b4.

tasks.title: Select and export the best RL candidate
tasks.summary: Choose the useful checkpoint, or explicitly retain theta0 when RL does not earn promotion.
steps: Rank valid RL checkpoints by held-out useful edits, restraint, termination and serving feasibility.
Merge the selected adapter once into a durable candidate and hash it with theta0 lineage.
Preserve the selected adapter, unmerged checkpoint and theta0/b4 fallbacks.
acceptance: One candidate ID or theta0 fallback is designated for release comparison.
The export has complete parent/tokenizer/renderer/reward lineage.
No final-set result was used to tune the selection.
tasks.stopRule: Stop export if no checkpoint is valid; promote theta0/b4 fallback and retain RL artifacts as experimental.

tasks.title: Finalize the sustained RL run and terminal archive
tasks.summary: After RL-08 decides stop or continue, finish or stop the trajectory at its gate, archive terminal state and close the 26-hour job.
tasks.effort: 0.25 engineer-hour; included in RL-05's 26 GPU-hour job
steps: Follow RL-08's stop/continue decision until the selected update target or Monday 00:00 cutoff.
Copy the latest full resumable state, final light adapter, telemetry and command line to durable storage.
Record terminal update, wall time, generated-token total, budget use and any recovery or early-stop reason.
acceptance: The terminal receipt states whether RL completed, stopped early or fell back.
The final checkpoint and latest full state are independently recoverable.
The 26 GPU-hour ceiling and Monday 00:00 cutoff are honored.
tasks.stopRule: Stop at Monday 00:00 or the 26 GPU-hour ceiling even if the target update count is incomplete.
tasks.gate: Required terminal receipt before RL candidate selection.

tasks.title: Admit the authenticated Anyscale auxiliary lane
tasks.summary: Verify that Anyscale can run a bounded same-parent SFT job with independent shutdown before uploading private artifacts.
steps: Confirm credentials, A10G allocation, region, private storage and shutdown API.
Set an all-in ceiling of $60 and an 18 allocation-hour maximum.
Record the exact image/environment and source snapshot required for parity.
acceptance: Auth and lifecycle controls pass without training.
The lane has a bounded cost and termination receipt.
No required local task depends on this lane.
tasks.stopRule: Stop the cloud branch after one failed admission or cost/lifecycle check; do not retry blindly.

tasks.title: Package theta0 and renderer for Anyscale
tasks.summary: Transfer the exact same parent, tokenizer, prompt contract and source fixes privately for the auxiliary SFT lane.
steps: Create a private manifest containing theta0 hashes, renderer ID, tokenizer and environment.
Upload only required artifacts and verify hashes in the cloud workspace.
Run one tokenizer/parser fixture before allocating training.
acceptance: Cloud and local theta0/renderer/tokenizer hashes match.
Private outputs have a durable download path.
The fixture passes before a GPU job is requested.
tasks.stopRule: Stop if hashes or source fixes differ; do not launch a non-equivalent branch.

tasks.title: Run the Anyscale 50-step SFT parity smoke
tasks.summary: Check the auxiliary SFT geometry and precision before using the cloud budget for breadth.
steps: Run the same prompt fixtures, LoRA geometry, effective batch and full-target checks.
Measure loss, trainable modules, memory, token profile and throughput.
Record the cloud precision and any data-loader difference.
acceptance: The smoke has finite loss, matching parser output and an explicit rate.
Precision/architecture differences are recorded rather than hidden.
The branch either passes or is dropped without affecting local delivery.
tasks.stopRule: Stop cloud training on fixture mismatch, nonfinite loss, uncontrolled cost or missing shutdown.

tasks.title: Run the Anyscale breadth SFT continuation
tasks.summary: Use authenticated cloud capacity for a same-parent replay plus validated underrepresented completion/repair families.
tasks.effort: 0.25 engineer-hour; up to 3,000 updates and 18 allocation-hours, capped at $60
steps: Launch from theta0 with the same renderer/tokenizer and LR 2e-5 after the parity smoke.
Use replay plus validated underrepresented families, with source caps and no final-set rows.
Save checkpoints and stop early if the local candidate already dominates or Monday 00:00 approaches.
acceptance: The branch has an independent checkpoint/readout and actual data mixture.
The cost and Monday cutoff are respected.
It is not treated as a required second primary lineage.
tasks.stopRule: Stop at the cost ceiling, no-data-signal gate or Monday 00:00; retain local theta0/RL as complete fallback.

tasks.title: Archive and shut down Anyscale artifacts
tasks.summary: Preserve cloud checkpoints and terminate resources before the deadline.
steps: If PAR-04 ran, copy manifests, logs, checkpoints and hashes to durable private storage.
If PAR-04 was disabled, record that no Anyscale resource or artifact existed; otherwise verify download integrity and actual cost.
Terminate instances and confirm no active resources remain.
acceptance: Selected cloud artifacts are recoverable locally, or a disabled/no-resource outcome is recorded.
The provider reports shutdown and final cost when a job ran.
No Anyscale process remains after Monday 00:00.
tasks.stopRule: Stop and escalate if shutdown cannot be independently verified; do not start another provider.
tasks.gate: Cleanup remains executable after a failed or interrupted training attempt. Record terminal failure separately from a valid trained artifact.

tasks.title: Decide whether a restrained cloud branch is justified
tasks.summary: Only admit a 25–30% no-op/finish-block curriculum branch if the rollout contract and reward are proven.
steps: Review parity, primary dev weaknesses and no-op/termination verifier coverage.
Choose SFT continuation as default; admit restrained RL only if cloud rollout parity is independently passed.
Write replacement budget and seed rules for any branch.
acceptance: The decision names the weakness being tested and common dev panel.
A restrained branch cannot silently add GPU-hours.
No branch is launched solely to occupy paid hardware.
tasks.stopRule: Stop branch admission when parity, verifier or budget replacement is absent.

tasks.title: Perform the one-shot Azure admission check
tasks.summary: Record the current Cost Management block and keep Azure out of the critical path unless authorization changes.
steps: Read subscription/provider status and Cost Management authorization once.
Record AADSTS530035 or the new authorized result with timestamp.
If blocked, close the task without launching or retrying.
acceptance: Azure status is unambiguous and independently timestamped.
No Azure spend occurs while Cost Management is blocked.
The local and Anyscale plans remain complete without Azure.
tasks.stopRule: Stop after the first blocked authorization result; no retries or dependent release work.

tasks.title: Evaluate eligible cloud branches on the common development panel
tasks.summary: Evaluate whichever auxiliary branches actually completed; an unavailable Azure or Anyscale branch must not prevent evaluating the other.
tasks.effort: 0.75 engineer-hour; up to 2 compute-hours on validated backend
steps: List completed auxiliary branch and shutdown receipts, and record unavailable or cut providers separately.
For each available branch, verify the exact theta0/tokenizer/renderer lineage and evaluate the common development panel.
Return eligible branch identities and metrics. If none completed, record that outcome and defer this optional comparison.
acceptance: Every evaluated branch has its own durable artifact and provider termination receipt.
Absent providers are explicit and do not block an available branch.
The comparison uses only development data and identifies which branches qualify for further work.
tasks.stopRule: Stop evaluation when branch artifacts or hashes are incomplete; retain unmerged local candidate.

tasks.title: Run a bounded Kaggle portable smoke
tasks.summary: Use remaining Kaggle quota only for portable compatibility, verifier or short SFT work after quota and precision checks.
steps: Recheck quota/reset and verify the standard-architecture image before allocation.
Run one portable tokenizer/generation or short SFT fixture without making it a release dependency.
Archive logs and shut down the notebook/job after the bounded smoke.
acceptance: Quota consumption and precision are recorded.
The smoke does not replace 5090 SFT/RL or alter the primary manifest.
No running Kaggle resource remains after the task.
tasks.stopRule: Stop on quota ambiguity, no-bf16/precision mismatch or any job exceeding its small budget.

tasks.title: Select branch inputs for optional merges or consolidation
tasks.summary: Decide whether any same-parent cloud branch complements RL before allocating the four-hour consolidation slot.
steps: Collect only auxiliary branches accepted by PAR-08 and the strongest local candidate.
Check same-parent tensor/tokenizer compatibility and complementary development gains; ignore missing or deferred providers.
Record the selected branch inputs, fixed blend coefficients and remaining consolidation budget, or defer merging with a reason.
acceptance: Only compatible same-parent branches can be nominated.
No optional branch is required for release.
The consolidation decision is fixed before any blend run.
tasks.stopRule: Stop merge planning if no branch has complementary development evidence or if it would consume final-validation time.

tasks.title: Run the conditional Azure restraint SFT
tasks.summary: If Azure admission succeeds, run the same-parent 20–25% no-op restraint continuation; if blocked, complete with a disabled receipt and no spend.
tasks.effort: 0.25 engineer-hour; up to 1,500 updates and 18 allocation-hours, capped at €100
steps: Check PAR-07's authorization outcome and exit with a disabled receipt when Cost Management remains blocked.
When authorized, launch from theta0 with replay plus validated no-op/positive-edit rows, BF16 where supported and LR 2e-5.
Save checkpoints, record actual cost and stop at 1,500 updates, €100 or Monday 00:00.
acceptance: A blocked Azure result causes no compute or spend and is usable by the branch DAG.
An authorized run uses theta0, the same renderer/tokenizer and a declared restraint mix.
The cost, update count and shutdown handoff are recorded.
tasks.stopRule: Stop immediately on blocked authorization, cost ceiling, missing lifecycle control or Monday 00:00; do not retry.
tasks.gate: The lead records a restraint weakness and a passing Azure admission before launch; this does not require Anyscale to be available.

tasks.title: Archive and shut down the Azure branch
tasks.summary: Close the Azure branch whether it ran or was disabled, preserving evidence and ensuring no resource remains.
steps: If PAR-11 ran, copy logs, checkpoints, hashes and cost records to durable private storage.
If PAR-11 was disabled, record the provider-disabled/no-resource outcome.
Terminate the instance and verify subscription/resource activity is zero.
acceptance: Azure artifacts are recoverable locally or the disabled outcome is explicit.
Final allocation cost and shutdown status are recorded.
No Azure resource remains after Monday 00:00.
tasks.stopRule: Stop and escalate if an Azure resource cannot be independently shut down; do not launch another provider.
tasks.gate: Cleanup remains executable after a failed Azure attempt. A termination receipt is required even when no usable adapter was produced.

tasks.title: Run up to three fixed same-parent blends
tasks.summary: Execute the predeclared blend coefficients only for eligible same-parent branch weights; retain theta0 and unmerged controls.
tasks.effort: 0.5 engineer-hour; 0 compute hours for weight arithmetic
steps: Materialize at most 0.75R+0.25B, 0.75R+0.25N and 0.50R+0.25B+0.25N when eligible.
Combine correctly scaled effective LoRA deltas or merged weights, never raw A/B factors.
Hash every blend and preserve theta0 plus each unmerged branch as controls.
acceptance: Only compatible parent/tokenizer/module mappings are blended.
No more than three actual blend artifacts are produced.
Missing or ineligible branches yield a no-blend receipt without GPU spend.
tasks.stopRule: Stop blending on incompatible tensors, missing branch hashes or any need for coefficient tuning.

tasks.title: Evaluate blends and unmerged branch controls
tasks.summary: Compare every blend with theta0, RL and each unmerged branch before allowing consolidation.
tasks.effort: 1 engineer-hour; up to 2 compute-hours on validated backend
steps: Score blends and unmerged controls on the common development panel by useful edit, no-op, parser, termination and latency.
Check parent/tokenizer/renderer hashes and keep final data unopened.
Nominate only a branch with complementary development evidence for the four-hour consolidation slot.
acceptance: Every candidate has common-panel denominators and lineage hashes.
The unmerged control is scored alongside every proposed blend.
No blend proceeds without a recorded complementary-gain decision.
tasks.stopRule: Stop if no branch is complementary or if evaluation would consume final-validation time.

tasks.title: Run matched consolidation and unmerged control
tasks.summary: Use the four-GPU-hour allowance for a short consolidation arm and a matched unmerged replay control only after PAR-14 earns it.
tasks.effort: 0.5 engineer-hour; up to 4 RTX 5090 GPU-hours total across both arms
steps: Run at most 500–1,000 SFT updates on the nominated blend with LR 1e-5 and cleaned training-only replay/harness data.
Run the matched unmerged branch control for the same updates, data, seed and optimizer budget.
Archive before/after adapters, optimizer state, source manifests and hashes.
acceptance: Both arms use training-only data and the same declared compute budget.
The four-GPU-hour consolidation ceiling is respected.
A post-consolidation evaluation can distinguish blending from another SFT stage.
tasks.stopRule: Stop both arms on quality regression, budget exhaustion, missing control or Monday 00:00; do not rescue a weak blend.
tasks.gate: Conditional and mutually exclusive with any target-draft adaptation budget replacement.

tasks.title: Evaluate consolidation and choose the branch
tasks.summary: Select the strongest unmerged, blended or consolidated candidate without making optional work a release dependency.
tasks.effort: 0.75 engineer-hour; up to 2 compute-hours on validated backend
steps: Score post-consolidation and unmerged controls on the common development panel.
Compare useful edits, no-op restraint, termination, retention and target-host feasibility.
Write a branch recommendation or no-adoption receipt for the release lead.
acceptance: The report contains pre/post and unmerged-control denominators.
A weak or inconclusive consolidation is discarded without further training.
The primary RL/theta0 fallback remains independently available.
tasks.stopRule: Stop on missing controls, final-data access or no measurable development benefit.
tasks.gate: Conditional; release can proceed without it.

tasks.title: Pin serving architecture and host placement
tasks.summary: Define the local/SSH extension host, llama.cpp version, server slot and target-host responsibilities before training finishes.
steps: Inspect extension host placement and the child llama-server launch path.
Pin llama.cpp b10453, one request slot, deterministic generation and the configured localhost port.
Record which host owns inference and how the notebook displays the workspace-host server.
acceptance: A host-placement and launch profile is reproducible.
The server/extension path has one explicit owner and fallback.
No server-to-notebook tunnel is assumed without a measured need.
tasks.stopRule: Stop if host placement cannot be observed or if two servers would contend for the same port.

tasks.title: Build the serving renderer and cache fixture
tasks.summary: Test the frozen prompt contract, source freshness, slot continuity and cached/fresh correctness independently of SFT/RL.
steps: Render representative current-buffer, history, evidence-missing and marker-like fixtures through the extension path.
Test cache-enabled versus fresh requests, slot identity, stale cancellation and response applicability.
Record prefix identity, context length and parser/application result for every event.
acceptance: Serving and training fixture IDs agree for the frozen contract.
Stale or out-of-date responses are rejected.
Cache reuse never overrides correctness or reuses old-checkpoint state.
tasks.stopRule: Stop if cached and fresh outputs disagree on correctness or if stale responses can apply.

tasks.title: Measure b4 target-host baseline
tasks.summary: Establish the fallback's full edit-cycle baseline on SSH/server and notebook paths before comparing a new checkpoint.
steps: Run b4 Q8_0 on CPU/server with one slot and the pinned parser/marker contract.
Collect p50/p95 time to a useful parsed suggestion, prefill, decode, cancellation and application time.
Record host load, context bucket, output tokens and exact greedy output.
acceptance: Baseline traces contain full-cycle timings rather than TTFT alone.
SSH/local placement and model hash are recorded.
The b4 fallback can be started fresh and as an existing sidecar.
tasks.stopRule: Stop timing claims if host contention or trace identity is missing; rerun only in a quiet declared window.

tasks.title: Profile cache, slot and stale-request behavior
tasks.summary: Measure serving architecture effects while weights and primary training continue separately.
steps: Exercise typing, cursor movement, history changes, diagnostics refresh, anchor moves and file switches.
Measure prefix-cache reuse, prompt recomputation, duplicate requests and stale cancellation.
Separate host-side index/cache timing from model prefix-cache timing.
acceptance: The report includes event-stratified reuse and correctness.
Anchor moves rebuild needed context rather than preserving stale source.
No cache speedup is presented as quality or lossless behavior.
tasks.stopRule: Stop a cache optimization when correctness or response applicability regresses.

tasks.title: Run bounded 2K/4K/8K latency traces
tasks.summary: Profile verified 2K/4K serving and retain 8K only as a stress/latency trace, not as supported edit-quality training.
steps: Render the same source/event traces under 2K and 4K profiles and the existing 8K stress band.
Reject overflow explicitly and record prompt/output tokens, context and host load.
Measure p50/p95 full-cycle latency, useful suggestion rate and parser correctness.
acceptance: The 8K trace is labeled stress/latency only.
No silent fallback to the extension's 8192 default occurs.
Results preserve b4 baseline comparability.
tasks.stopRule: Stop a larger default profile if target support, quality or latency is not verified.

tasks.title: Inspect competing draft and speculative pathways
tasks.summary: Compare ngram/copy, released or adapted DSpark, small autoregressive drafts and attached-head/MTP candidates; do not assume DSpark is best.
steps: Read the speculative-paths design and inspect available ngram/copy, DSpark, small-AR and attached-head/MTP artifacts for tokenizer, architecture and llama.cpp coupling.
Compare target/draft vocabulary, layers, dimensions, marker/stop behavior and expected integration cost with the MiniCPM family.
Rank pathways by early cheap-science value and write a theta0/final-candidate acceptance gate for each.
acceptance: The receipt distinguishes official artifact facts, local artifact facts and hypotheses.
No pathway is selected from model name or stock acceptance alone.
The gate states which candidates can be tested after theta0 and which require target-specific adaptation.
tasks.stopRule: Stop any pathway whose tokenizer/architecture coupling or source artifact cannot be established; retain ordinary serving.

tasks.title: Run baseline draft acceptance after theta0
tasks.summary: Test each cheap compatible draft pathway against the actual merged theta0 before considering target-matched adaptation.
steps: Run theta0 with no draft and each compatible ngram/copy, DSpark or attached-head pathway on short and long fixtures.
Compare accepted tokens, greedy output, parser correctness, no-op behavior and end-to-end cycle time.
Record target/draft hashes and failures by context/event.
acceptance: Acceptance and correctness are measured on theta0, not inferred from stock checkpoints.
Any output mismatch or crash is preserved in the receipt.
The receipt ranks candidates for a small target-matched adaptation or rejection.
tasks.stopRule: Stop draft promotion on any correctness mismatch, crash or unmeasured target/draft pairing.

tasks.title: Run target-matched draft adaptation only by budget replacement
tasks.summary: If a pathway is viable, prepare target-matched draft work from theta0 under a replacement budget; refresh acceptance against final target weights later.
tasks.effort: 1 engineer-hour; replacement budget only, 0 incremental campaign hours
steps: Use RUN-07 to choose the best feasible target-matched draft path rather than assuming DSpark wins. Read SPECULATIVE-PATHS.md and prove its training and export path fits the budget.
Record the exact budget transfer; freeze a theta0 or later target snapshot, and prepare target-generated training-split data only. Evaluation/S1 traces stay excluded.
Train or adapt within the transferred allowance, keeping the target fixed for that draft stage. It may run while main RL continues on independent admitted hardware.
After the final target is selected, measure compatibility and acceptance again; refresh only if worthwhile and still inside the same transferred budget. Leave final promotion to RUN-10.
acceptance: The replacement ledger shows zero added GPU/credit hours.
Target/draft hashes, theta0 adaptation stage and data provenance are recorded.
Final promotion requires unchanged correctness and measured cycle-time improvement after the late refresh.
tasks.stopRule: Stop if target/renderer compatibility, usable training/export support or the budget transfer is missing. No extra hours are implied; skip refresh if the original pair still passes final checks.
tasks.gate: Complete the at-most-90-engineer-minute training/export feasibility check; reassign at most two GPU-hours from optional consolidation, or capacity within an existing cloud ceiling, including any final refresh.

tasks.title: Run the bounded notebook CPU/Vulkan scout
tasks.summary: Compare notebook CPU and Vulkan/iGPU behavior for the fallback or available finalist without turning it into a training dependency.
steps: Run identical Q8 model, trace set, output cap and parser on CPU and Vulkan.
Measure full-cycle p50/p95 and stability under representative context events.
Keep Vulkan only if it gives a substantial stable end-to-end gain; otherwise retain CPU.
acceptance: Host, model hash, traces and load are recorded.
The decision uses full-cycle timing, not raw decode alone.
No notebook path becomes a release dependency without a quiet-window smoke.
tasks.stopRule: Stop after 90 minutes or on instability; do not train a draft head.

tasks.title: Run final retargeted draft acceptance and end-to-end benchmark
tasks.summary: Benchmark the selected final Q8 target with baseline and every admitted speculative pathway, reporting correctness before speed.
steps: Run the final target with no draft and each admitted ngram/copy, DSpark, small-AR or attached-head arm under identical 2K/4K traces plus selected 8K stress.
Check exact greedy outputs, parser/no-op correctness, crashes, changing-context behavior, accepted tokens and end-to-end p50/p95.
Promote speculation only when measured benefit meets the predeclared gate; otherwise package ordinary serving.
acceptance: The final report includes target/draft hashes and paired correctness outcomes.
No lossless speed or acceptance is assumed; any mismatch disqualifies that draft.
The release has a measured baseline fallback.
tasks.stopRule: Stop draft promotion on any mismatch, crash, p95 regression or absent measured speedup; ordinary serving remains valid.

tasks.title: Close training and optional-branch decisions
tasks.summary: Select only completed, validated artifacts and close unfinished optional work before freezing the release. A failed new lineage still permits an honest b4 delivery.
steps: At the Monday cutoff, inspect real process/provider state and the accepted SFT, RL, cloud, draft and consolidation receipts.
Record every optional branch as accepted, cut or unavailable. Require terminal artifacts for any proposed candidate, and terminate campaign allocations through their owner.
If the new lineage is blocked or fails development gates, select the verified b4 fallback with its matched renderer. Keep failed tasks visibly blocked instead of marking unperformed work complete.
Write the candidate inventory and close further weight/harness changes before REL-01; do not wait for an unavailable provider.
acceptance: Every candidate is an immutable, terminal artifact with its own development evidence and renderer.
Optional work and live resource ownership have explicit dispositions; active training is not mistaken for a completed checkpoint.
There is at least one eligible candidate, including b4 if necessary, and no final-test result was used for selection.
tasks.stopRule: Keep the final set sealed if no verifiable artifact exists. Resolve the saved b4 rollback before claiming a deliverable.
tasks.gate: Monday 00:00 ends main RL/cloud allocation; Monday 12:00 freezes weights and harness. This decision accepts available evidence without requiring every optional branch.

tasks.title: Freeze development ranking and finalist set
tasks.summary: Select the primary candidate, SFT/theta0 fallback and any eligible branch before opening final data.
steps: Collect SFT, RL, banked comparator and runtime development receipts.
Rank useful edit/completion, no-op restraint, termination, tokenizer retention and latency.
Freeze at most two finalists for final evaluation, with b4 fallback and no cloud dependency.
acceptance: Finalist IDs and fallback are fixed before final-set access.
All ranking inputs have denominators and lineage hashes.
No final-test failure is used to retune the ranking.
tasks.stopRule: Stop if no candidate has valid development evidence; promote b4 fallback and document the missing new lineage.

tasks.title: Prepare the locked-final execution gate
tasks.summary: Verify final manifest integrity and schedule access only after the Monday 12:00 weight/harness freeze.
steps: Verify final manifest hash, source exclusions, package groups and evaluator version.
Record the freeze timestamp and finalist/model/harness hashes.
Prepare quality, intent/preference, BPB and latency commands without reading final rows.
acceptance: The final set remains unread before the declared freeze.
The gate names exact finalists and evaluator commands.
A failed integrity check blocks final scoring.
tasks.stopRule: Stop final access if the manifest or evaluator has changed since DAT-08.

tasks.title: Run the locked final quality battery
tasks.summary: Score finalists on exact, semantic/useful edit, no-op, parser and termination behavior after freeze.
tasks.effort: 2 engineer-hours; up to 4 compute-hours after freeze
steps: Open the locked final set only after Monday 12:00 and run every finalist with the frozen renderer/stop contract.
Record exact and semantic results, no-op false suggestions, invalid/cap rates and denominators by package/family.
Bootstrap intervals by package or trajectory and preserve raw outputs.
acceptance: The report contains locked-set provenance and no pre-freeze access.
Every score has a denominator and failure category.
No weights, prompt layout or harness policy changes after REL-02 are permitted during final scoring.
The result can be reproduced from finalist and evaluator hashes.
tasks.stopRule: Stop and fall back if final rows are contaminated, evaluator hashes differ or a candidate fails parser integrity.

tasks.title: Run blinded final intent and preference evaluation
tasks.summary: Compare the strongest finalist(s) with b4 using visible prompt context, both orders and valid-pair accounting.
tasks.effort: 1.5 engineer-hours; up to 3 compute-hours after freeze
steps: Generate candidate proposals on the declared final intent/trajectory subset with blinded labels.
Run both orders with known-good/corrupted controls and record ties, order conflicts and invalid calls separately.
Collect at most 300 paired points per contrast or report an honest shortfall.
acceptance: At least 200 valid both-order comparisons are sought or the shortfall is explicit.
No b4 label is reused for an O2/new-candidate proposal.
Preference and intent outcomes remain separate from deterministic exact scores.
No weight or harness changes occur after the final set opens.
tasks.stopRule: Stop judging on provider failure or invalid controls; do not call an invalid sample a pass.
tasks.gate: Required when provider/human review is available; report shortfall.

tasks.title: Run retention, BPB and tokenizer-specific guards
tasks.summary: Check general-R/text retention within tokenizer and compare target-host behavior without cross-tokenizer loss claims.
tasks.effort: 1 engineer-hour; up to 2 compute-hours after freeze
steps: Run identical-byte general-R/text BPB and parent-retention diagnostics for each finalist.
Report new-family own-starting-checkpoint retention and b4 comparison separately.
Join no-op/quality/length and latency diagnostics into the promotion table.
acceptance: Token loss is compared only within one tokenizer.
Any >1% b4-descendant degradation is diagnosed before promotion.
Retention cannot override materially better or worse measured editing without disclosure.
The architecture/profile identity is frozen for the final measurement.
tasks.stopRule: Stop promotion when tokenizer identity or baseline comparison is missing.

tasks.title: Run final SSH/local editor smoke
tasks.summary: Verify the selected model, frozen harness and ordinary serving path in the actual editor before quantization/promotion.
steps: Start the external sidecar fresh and connect the extension on the workspace host.
Exercise typing, cursor movement, history, no-op and file-switch episodes under the selected context profile.
Measure p50/p95 useful suggestion time and compare with same-host b4.
acceptance: The editor applies only current-buffer-valid responses.
Latency and parser results are recorded for real events.
The candidate stays within the declared slowdown/quality rule or b4 is retained.
tasks.stopRule: Stop promotion on stale application, parser failure, crash or unexplained p95 regression.

tasks.title: Export the candidate Q8_0 GGUF before final evaluation
tasks.summary: Export and hash the selected deployment artifact before opening the final set, so quality and latency checks assess the same candidate that will ship.
steps: Convert the selected full/merged weights to pinned llama.cpp b10453 Q8_0.
Hash GGUF, tokenizer, prompt/serving manifest and source environment.
Run a small greedy/parser/no-op quality smoke against the pre-quantized finalist.
acceptance: The GGUF loads on the target host and hash is recorded.
Quantization smoke preserves output contract and parser behavior.
The artifact has a rollback b4 path.
tasks.stopRule: Stop export on load/hash/quality mismatch; retain the unquantized finalist and b4.
tasks.gate: Use the frozen candidate and renderer; export does not authorize further target-weight adaptation.

tasks.title: Assemble lineage, rollback and installation package
tasks.summary: Package all evidence needed for a reviewer or future operator to reproduce and revert the release.
steps: Write base revision→SFT→theta0→RL/adaptation/branch lineage with hashes and stage IDs.
Bundle raw scores, denominators, uncertainty, prompt/data manifests, environment and target-host traces.
Add fresh-start and running-sidecar installation commands plus b4 rollback.
acceptance: Every released file maps to a source, parent, tokenizer and evaluator hash.
The package contains both selected artifact and rollback configuration.
No private source or cloud credential is included.
tasks.stopRule: Stop package publication if any hash, denominator or rollback path is absent.

tasks.title: Apply the promotion gate or select b4 fallback
tasks.summary: Make the final quality/latency decision against predeclared thresholds without tuning on final failures.
steps: Check clustered exact/semantic, no-op, preference/intent, retention and latency thresholds.
Select the new candidate only when its benefit and guardrails are supported; otherwise select b4.
Record inconclusive dimensions and keep all rejected artifacts as experimental.
acceptance: One recommended model/harness/runtime combination is named.
The fallback decision cites thresholds, denominators and uncertainty.
No final-set failure causes another training or prompt change.
tasks.stopRule: Stop all tuning after the final test; b4 is the release if any hard gate fails.

tasks.title: Deliver the Tuesday package and tracker snapshot
tasks.summary: Verify installation, update the local persistent tracker and create the final hosted-readable details snapshot by 09:00 Berlin.
steps: Test the selected artifact from a fresh start and an already-running sidecar using the packaged commands.
Copy hashes, receipts, rollback instructions and known limitations to the private delivery location.
Update the local interactive tracker and render an expandable hosted snapshot without a PostPlanCSP script.
acceptance: The package is installable and its hashes match the promotion receipt.
The final tracker/snapshot identifies delivery time, owner, artifact and fallback.
Delivery is complete by 2026-09-15 09:00+02:00 or an explicit recovery receipt names the blocker.
tasks.stopRule: Stop publication of any public/private artifact if integrity or privacy checks fail; retain local delivery and b4 rollback.
